_note: Original advanced concept questions for sliding window.

questions.title: Window meaning
questions.prompt: What does a sliding window represent?
questions.explanation: The window is the current slice of data being tracked.
choices: The current range between left and right

questions.title: Shrink rule
questions.prompt: When should the left side of a sliding window usually move?
questions.explanation: Moving left shrinks the current window until it becomes valid again.
questions.code:
window sum = 9
limit = 6

The rule is broken.
choices: When the current window breaks the rule
Before the right side ever moves

questions.title: Trace a window
questions.prompt: What should happen before keeping 4 in a sum-limited window?
questions.explanation: The window must shrink from the left when the running sum is too large.
questions.code:
nums = [2, 1, 4]
limit = 3
window starts empty
add 2, add 1, next adding 4 is too large
choices: Move left and subtract old values until the rule is true

questions.title: Running total
questions.prompt: After the window shrinks, what is total?
questions.explanation: Add the right value first, then subtract values removed from the left. 2 + 1 + 4 is 7, then subtract 2 to get 5.
questions.code:
nums = [2, 1, 4]
limit = 5
add 2, add 1, add 4
total = 7
remove nums[left] which is 2

questions.title: Fixed-size window
questions.prompt: For a fixed-size window of 3, what happens after adding the 4th item?
questions.explanation: A fixed-size window removes the item that falls off the left so only 3 items remain.
questions.code:
window size should stay 3
current window has 4 items

questions.title: Negative number caveat
questions.prompt: Why can sum-based sliding window fail with negative numbers?
questions.explanation: Negative numbers can make the sum drop after adding a value, so the simple grow/shrink rule may no longer be reliable.
questions.code:
nums may contain negative numbers
window sum can go down when right moves
choices: The sum may not move in one predictable direction
The list cannot be looped over

questions.title: Sliding window loop
questions.prompt: Arrange the common sliding window steps.
questions.explanation: A window grows on the right, shrinks on the left, and updates the answer when valid.
lines: Set left to 0 and current state to empty.
Add the new right-side item to the state.
While the window breaks the rule, remove the left-side item and move left.
Update the best answer when the window is valid.

questions.title: Stale state bug
questions.prompt: What bug happens if `left` moves but the running sum is not updated?
questions.explanation: The stored sum no longer describes the actual window, so later decisions use stale information.
questions.code:
left += 1
# forgot to subtract the old left value
choices: The stored sum no longer matches the window
